projects.title: Code Buddy
projects.tags: Multi-agent systems · LLM tooling · Developer experience
bullets: Architected a multi-agent GenAI code-review platform deployed across 4,000+ repos for 12,000+ engineers , running detect-then-fix agents under a tool-calling orchestrator that generate self-validating fixes and pass validation guardrails before posting.
Scaled the platform to 2M+ automated code reviews (180,000+ monthly), with a modeled estimate of 114,000+ engineer-hours saved per month .
Cut review-retrieval latency via a Tree-sitter symbolic-retrieval layer over a ccls/ctags dependency graph with TTL symbol caching.
Built SlideGen , an LLM tool that turns raw technical data into corporate-compliant decks using structured-output validation and template-aware layout.
Built an agentic tool that reads live C/C++ modem source and drives interactive 4G/5G NAS protocol tests through a 14-tool calling loop, no hardcoded answer mappings.

Built an autonomous LLM agent that triages NAS modem hotline escalations end-to-end via a 13-tool calling loop: parses issue emails, searches Perforce source and CR/JIRA databases, and shelves a 3GPP-cited candidate fix after a 4-model consensus review.

Built evaluation workflows for code-review agents using golden code changes and precision/recall comparisons. Worked on structural code retrieval so agents could look up symbols and dependencies instead of relying on lexical search alone.
projects.headline: From a pilot to 12,000 engineers.
projects.summary: A multi-agent code-review platform I architected at Qualcomm, built to detect issues, generate verifiable fixes, and scale across 4,000+ repositories.

projects.title: CabinAI
projects.tags: Multi-Agent VLA, On-Device AI, LLM · SparQ Qualcomm TechFest 2026
bullets: Architected a 7-agent hybrid edge-cloud vision-language-action system: safety and voice run on-device, while complex reasoning can escalate to Qwen3-VL-32B / gpt-oss-20b on Qualcomm AIC100.
Designed a core drowsiness detection pipeline utilizing a 3-engine vote consensus (rule-based, ML, and LLM) to drastically reduce false positives.
Developed ZeroClaw, a state orchestration bus tying all agents with a location-aware voice assistant into a shared, proactive intelligence layer.
Demonstrated the system end-to-end via a full driving simulation through Gachibowli, Hyderabad.
Jury Award Winner at SparQ Qualcomm TechFest 2026 , competing solo against 166 teams.
Implemented a deterministic edge/cloud router with multi-tier fallbacks. Routing 80%+ of queries locally was the design target; the distribution depends on the workload.
Implemented local retrieval over a 31-document corpus with BGE-small ONNX embeddings and a keyword fallback, without a PyTorch runtime dependency.
projects.headline: Driver intelligence, one step ahead.
projects.summary: A hybrid edge-cloud system that brings seven agents together to anticipate driver fatigue and keep safety decisions close to the device.

projects.title: HealthSense
projects.tags: Foundation Model, Wearable AI, PyTorch · SparQ Qualcomm TechFest 2026
bullets: Built a prototype dashboard and agent pipeline for ECG, EEG, PPG, EMG, and IMU signals. Implemented signal-processing heuristics and a small PyTorch 1D ECG CNN with ONNX export.
Explored a PanLUNA-inspired multimodal foundation-model design. The 5.4M-parameter architecture and 95 ms / 19 mJ NPU figures were concept targets, rather than measurements of a deployed model.

Demonstrated the BioTrain adaptation workflow through simulated training curves; on-device backpropagation remained future work. ECG experiments were exploratory and were not subject-held-out clinical validation.
projects.headline: Exploring intelligence for wearable signals.
projects.summary: A biosignal-system prototype combining a small ECG CNN, signal-processing heuristics, and an agent dashboard. Inspired by multimodal wearable foundation models.

projects.title: MyAI
projects.tags: On-Device LLM, Android, Hexagon NPU · SparQ Qualcomm TechFest 2026
bullets: Built an Android assistant with a four-tier routing design: deterministic keyword matching, response caching, local tools, and Genie-backed model inference. In the public implementation, the two model tiers share a runtime callback.
Tested a quantized Qwen2.5-VL-7B bundle on Snapdragon 8 Elite through Qualcomm Genie. The public source requires external Genie runtime artifacts for the NPU path.
Shipped the default APK without INTERNET permission and added a Gradle build guard against accidentally introducing it.
Implemented local calculator, datetime, calendar, contacts, and alarm tools with structured JSON calls.
projects.headline: Your assistant. Your device.
projects.summary: An Android assistant that routes between tools, cache, and quantized language models—with no internet permission.

projects.title: Digital Twin - MapMyIndia
bullets: Initialized a Unity map from a location provider and implemented mouse-look, movement, and zoom controls.
Built a navigation coroutine that zooms out, interpolates between coordinates, then restores zoom so distant map transitions retain spatial context.

The recorded demo and original project title use MapMyIndia terminology; the public repository uses the Mapbox SDK. This is an interactive geographic viewer, rather than a synchronized live physical twin.
The original project notes also describe map-layer inspector tooling for marker and model management, alongside zoom and rotation controls.
projects.headline: Navigate a map in three dimensions.
projects.summary: A Unity geospatial viewer with location initialization, tiled maps, and smooth coordinate-to-coordinate navigation. The public implementation uses Mapbox and C#.

projects.title: Compiler Construction
bullets: Built a compiler front end as a team project in C, with a DFA twin-buffer lexer and a table-driven LL(1) parser using FIRST/FOLLOW sets.
Constructed an AST and symbol tables, with scope/type checks, partial semantic analysis, and panic-mode error recovery. Executable code generation was not completed.
Compared parse-tree and AST node storage: one sample showed roughly 70% lower estimated node-structure memory, calculated from node counts and structure sizes.
projects.headline: Inside a compiler front end.
projects.summary: A team-built compiler front end in C: twin-buffer lexing, LL(1) parsing, AST construction, symbol tables, and semantic analysis.

projects.title: Live Train Status
bullets: Modeled trains, stations, ordered schedules, routes, and delays in SQL. Used relational queries and views to find possible journeys and derive arrival estimates.
Built Flutter lookup, status, and admin delay screens consuming JSON endpoints. This is a coursework prototype; the original hosted backend is not presented as a currently operating service.
projects.headline: From a relational schema to a train journey.
projects.summary: A Flutter and SQL coursework prototype connecting train discovery, schedules, route queries, and delay-management screens.

recommendations.name: Kiran Janga
recommendations.preview: Varun is an exceptionally talented engineer with a clear vision for the future of AI, and I wish him nothing but the best in his future endeavors.
paragraphs: I had the pleasure of working with Varun Sahni on developing GenAI tooling for software engineering. Varun demonstrated remarkable foresight in identifying how design patterns can be used to write scalable app. We took a GenAI-powered code review assistant from a pilot phase to mass adoption, purposefully designing it with a future-proof architecture that ensured scalability as usage grew.

Beyond his core contributions, Varun’s relentless drive for innovation was evident in his development of an AI-powered presentation builder and a sophisticated on-device assistant prototype. His ability to turn ambitious concepts into functional, high-impact products, often under the pressure of hackathons and competitive demo selections, truly sets him apart. Varun is an exceptionally talented engineer with a clear vision for the future of AI, and I wish him nothing but the best in his future endeavors.

posts.title: The Voice Agent Problem Nobody Talks About
posts.excerpt: When you talk to a voice agent, the hard part is not transcription or synthesis. The hard part is what happens when you interrupt it mid-sentence, or pause to think and then keep talking, or when two people speak at once. Real conversations are messy. They have false starts, interruptions, and moments where you change your mind halfway through a sentence.

posts.title: How Claude Learned to Watch Videos: The Decomposition Pattern for Multimodal AI Agents
posts.excerpt: Claude can read a webpage. It can run a script. It can browse a repository. What it cannot do, out of the box, is watch a video. You paste a YouTube link and it has to either guess from the title or pull a transcript that is missing 90% of what is on screen.

posts.title: Building Code Buddy: A Multi-Agent GenAI Code Review Platform at Qualcomm
posts.excerpt: At Qualcomm, I had the opportunity to architect Code Buddy , a multi-agent GenAI code-review platform that's now deployed across 4,000+ repositories and serves 12,000+ engineers. Here's the story of how we built it, the architecture decisions that mattered, and what we learned along the way.
